oauth-login-contract.proposal:
# Proposal: OAuth Login Contract

Define the shared HTTP contract every implementation slice consumes (token issuance, OAuth redirect, refresh). The contract slice is projectless — its baseline is `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` after merge.

## Why

Login currently lives only on the web client; routing native + mobile clients through the same provider requires a stable HTTP shape both implementation slices can lock in.

## Outcome

A `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` baseline both implementation slices `depends-on:`.
oauth-login-contract.spec:
# Spec: OAuth Login Contract

The contract slice authors the HTTP shape for token issuance, redirect, and refresh. Implementation slices read this baseline; they MUST NOT redeclare or extend the contract YAML inline.

## Endpoints

- `POST /auth/oauth/start` — opens a provider session, returns redirect URL.
- `GET /auth/oauth/callback` — handles provider redirect, mints a session token.
- `POST /auth/oauth/refresh` — rotates a refresh token.

The full YAML schema lives at `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` after merge.

add-oauth-tokens.proposal:
# Proposal: add-oauth-tokens

Implement OAuth provider integration + token persistence in the `shop-backend` Omnia project. Depends on the OAuth login contract slice — references baseline `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` for the HTTP shape.

## Why

Native + mobile clients need a backend that handles OAuth callbacks, persists provider tokens, and rotates refresh tokens server-side.

## Outcome

A new `oauth_tokens` Omnia crate that exposes the three endpoints from `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` and persists tokens.
add-oauth-tokens.spec:
# Spec: add-oauth-tokens

Reads baseline `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` and exposes its endpoints from the Omnia runtime.

## Storage

Per-user `oauth_session` rows keyed by provider id; refresh tokens encrypted at rest.

## Failure modes

Replay-resistant nonce on `/auth/oauth/start`; idempotent `/auth/oauth/refresh`.

add-oauth-tokens.design:
# Design: add-oauth-tokens

Reads baseline `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` (the merged contract slice) — the implementation slice does NOT author new contract YAML inline, it depends-on the contract slice and consumes the baseline.

## Provider integration

Uses the Omnia HTTP runtime's `serve` adapter to bind the three contract endpoints. The provider client lives in `crates/oauth_tokens/src/provider.rs`; tokens are encrypted with the platform key before persistence.

## Token rotation

The `/auth/oauth/refresh` endpoint is idempotent against the refresh token; replays return the same access token until the original expires.

add-oauth-screens.proposal:
# Proposal: add-oauth-screens

Implement the iOS + Android login UI and OAuth redirect handling in the `shop-mobile` Vectis project. Depends on the OAuth login contract slice — references baseline `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` for the HTTP shape both clients call.

## Why

The mobile clients need login screens that talk to the backend's OAuth endpoints (defined in the contract slice) and persist sessions client-side.

## Outcome

A new `LoginScreen` Vectis shell with OAuth provider buttons, redirect handler, and refresh-token storage.
add-oauth-screens.spec:
# Spec: add-oauth-screens

Reads baseline `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` for endpoint URLs + payloads. Calls them from a Vectis shell.

## Screens

- `LoginScreen` — provider-button list.
- `OAuthCallbackScreen` — handles provider redirect, hands token to the session store.
- `LoggedInScreen` — surfaces a logged-in indicator.

## Token storage

iOS Keychain / Android Keystore via the Vectis platform adapter.

add-oauth-screens.design:
# Design: add-oauth-screens

Reads baseline `contracts/oauth-login.yaml` (the merged contract slice). The implementation slice does NOT author new contract YAML inline; it depends-on the contract slice and consumes the baseline.

## Vectis shell layout

The `LoginScreen` shell composes platform-specific provider-button widgets via the Vectis adapter pattern — iOS via `UIKit`, Android via `Jetpack Compose`. Both clients hit the same `POST /auth/oauth/start` endpoint defined by the contract slice.

## Refresh

The shared `TokenStore` adapter persists refresh tokens in the platform secure store and refreshes the access token via the contract's `/auth/oauth/refresh` endpoint when the access token expires.
